nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with finite state set $Q$, this is the set $F \subseteq Q$ of accepting states of $M$, as a finite set.
nodes.title: Block of accepting states

nodes.summary: The bound for the complete terminating minimization execution. `DFA.hopcroftLoop_waiting_eq_nil` proves this fuel exhausts the queue; `hopcroftLoop_eq_hopcroftLoop_of_length` ties the trace to its result.
nodes.title: Predecessor-work bound for the complete Hopcroft run

nodes.summary: Double counting visits by source state and letter, retaining every incoming transition even when many sources have the same successor.
nodes.title: Hopcroft predecessor-work as splitter counts plus pops

nodes.summary: An empty alphabet causes no predecessor-work, for any state count.
nodes.title: Zero Hopcroft predecessor-work over an empty alphabet

nodes.summary: Zero predecessor-work for zero/one-state boundary parameters. This does not assert that constructing the initial partition costs zero.
nodes.title: Zero Hopcroft predecessor-work with at most one state

nodes.summary: A uniform `O(|Σ| n log n)` bound, with the explicit constant `4`. The condition `n ≥ 2` is essential when absorbing the additive unit into the logarithm. This concerns predecessor-work, not scan runtime.
nodes.title: $O(|\Sigma| n \log n)$ bound on Hopcroft predecessor-work

nodes.summary: Total predecessor-work bound, including one unit for every pop, for every prefix of the initialized execution. No runtime claim is made for the scanning implementation or for initialization.
nodes.title: Total predecessor-work bound

nodes.summary: The predecessor cost of a splitter trace: for each popped splitter `(C, a)`, one predecessor visit per state in the preimage `preimage M C a`, plus `1` per-splitter overhead. This is the quantity the total-work bound constrains to `O(|Σ| n log n)`. Charging splitter size `C.card` instead would undercount: if all `n` states transition on `a` to one state `q`, processing the singleton splitter `({q}, a)` costs `n`…
nodes.title: Predecessor cost of a Hopcroft splitter trace

nodes.summary: The trace and the loop take the same number of steps: the trace length is the fuel the loop consumed, i.e. the loop would stop after exactly that many rounds if run with only that much fuel.
nodes.title: Hopcroft splitter trace length equals loop fuel

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finite state set $Q$ over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, let $P$ be a partition of the states given as a list of blocks, let $W$ be a waiting list of splitters, and let $k$ be a natural number. If $P$ and $W$ satisfy the invariants of Hopcroft's loop and $|W| + |\Sigma| \cdot (|Q| - |P|) \le k$, where $|P|$ and $|W|$ are the lengths of the lists, then Hopcroft's loop run from $(P, W)$ with a…
nodes.title: Termination of Hopcroft's loop

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finite state set $Q$ over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$. Hopcroft's loop, run from the initial partition and the initial waiting list with a budget of $|\Sigma| \cdot (|Q| + 1)$ rounds, ends with an empty waiting list.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's waiting list is exhausted

nodes.summary: At the proved terminating fuel, instrumentation returns the original correct minimization partition and an empty waiting list.
nodes.title: Instrumented complete Hopcroft run returns the minimization partition

nodes.summary: The canonical cost monad records the proved total predecessor-work bound for every initialized execution prefix.
nodes.title: Recorded Hopcroft cost obeys the predecessor-work bound

nodes.summary: Instrumentation preserves the exact loop result.
nodes.title: Instrumented Hopcroft loop returns the original result

nodes.summary: The recorded cost is exactly the work of the actual popped trace.
nodes.title: Recorded Hopcroft cost equals the work of the popped trace

nodes.summary: The actual loop with predecessor-visit and pop events recorded in CSLib's `TimeM`. Pure scans are not charged in this event model.
nodes.title: Hopcroft loop with recorded predecessor-work

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA. Given a round budget $k$, a partition $P$ of the states of $M$ (a list of blocks) and a waiting list $W$ of splitters $(C, a)$, each a block $C$ with a letter $a$, the loop returns the pair $(P, W)$ unchanged if $k = 0$ or $W$ is empty. Otherwise it removes the first splitter $(C, a)$ from $W$, replaces $P$ by the partition after the splitter $(C, a)$ and the remaining waiting list by the waiting…
nodes.title: Hopcroft's refinement loop

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finite state set $Q$ over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$. Hopcroft's partition of $M$ is the partition returned by Hopcroft's loop run from the initial partition and the initial waiting list with a budget of $|\Sigma| \cdot (|Q| + 1)$ rounds.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's partition

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$ with finitely many states over a finite alphabet, Hopcroft's relation of $M$, the set of pairs of states lying in a common block of Hopcroft's partition, equals Moore's state equivalence of $M$ as a set of pairs of states.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's partition is Moore's relation

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with finitely many states, Hopcroft's relation is the set of pairs $(p, q)$ of states of $M$ such that $p$ and $q$ lie in a common block of Hopcroft's partition.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's relation

nodes.summary: The loop and the trace recurse on the same state, so they take the same number of steps. The two theorems below make the correspondence usable: the trace length is at most `k`, and running the loop for exactly the trace's length gives the full loop result, so the trace contains every splitter the loop pops and no others.
nodes.title: The splitter trace records exactly the splitters the loop pops

nodes.summary: The splitters popped by Hopcroft's loop, in order: the same recursion as `DFA.hopcroftLoop`, collecting each popped splitter. The cost of processing one popped splitter `(C, a)` is `(preimage M C a).card + 1`: one predecessor visit per state whose `a`-successor lies in `C`, plus `O(1)` per-splitter overhead. See `hopcroftCost`. `hopcroftLoop_eq_hopcroftLoop_of_length` proves this trace records exactly the splitters…
nodes.title: Trace of splitters popped by Hopcroft's algorithm

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with finite state set $Q$ and set of accepting states $F$, the initial partition is the list of blocks $F$, $Q \setminus F$, in this order, with any empty block removed.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's initial partition

nodes.summary: With at most one state, the accepting/rejecting split has an empty side, so the algorithm has no initial splitters.
nodes.title: No initial Hopcroft splitters with at most one state

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with finite state set $Q$, set of accepting states $F$ and finite alphabet $\Sigma$. If $F$ and $Q \setminus F$ are both nonempty, the initial waiting list consists of the splitters $(S, b)$ for every letter $b \in \Sigma$, where $S = F$ if $|F| \le |Q \setminus F|$ and $S = Q \setminus F$ otherwise; if one of $F$ and $Q \setminus F$ is empty, the initial waiting list is empty.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's initial waiting list

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$ with finitely many states over a finite alphabet, Hopcroft's initial partition and initial waiting list satisfy the invariants of Hopcroft's loop.
nodes.title: The invariants hold initially

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with transition function $\delta$. A list $P$ of sets of states and a waiting list $W$ of pairs $(C, b)$ of a set of states $C$ and a letter $b$ satisfy the invariants when: (i) $P$ is a partition of the states into nonempty blocks; (ii) for every $(C, b)$ in $W$, $C$ is an entry of $P$; (iii) for every letter $b$ and all states $p$, $q$ lying in a common entry of $P$, if for every $C$ with…
nodes.title: Invariants of Hopcroft's loop

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$, Hopcroft's final partition of $M$ is a partition of the states of $M$ into nonempty blocks.
nodes.title: Hopcroft's final partition is a partition

nodes.summary: A list $P$ of sets of states is a partition into nonempty blocks when entries of $P$ at different positions are disjoint, every entry of $P$ is nonempty, and every state lies in some entry of $P$.
nodes.title: Partitions of the states

nodes.summary: A nonempty popped block pays for its pop, even if its preimage is empty. This bounds the `+1` term independently of predecessor visits.
nodes.title: Number of pops bounded by the total splitter count

nodes.summary: If a list $P$ of sets of states is a partition into nonempty blocks, then the length of $P$ is at most the number $|Q|$ of states.
nodes.title: A partition has at most as many blocks as there are states

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with transition function $\delta$, let $P$ be a list of sets of states, $C$ a set of states and $a$ a letter, and let $\mathrm{pre} = \{q : \delta(q, a) \in C\}$. The partition after the splitter $(C, a)$, which replaces each entry $D$ of $P$ meeting both $\mathrm{pre}$ and its complement by $D \cap \mathrm{pre}$ and $D \setminus \mathrm{pre}$, has length equal to the length of $P$ plus the number…
nodes.title: Number of blocks after one round

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with transition function $\delta$ over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, let $P$ be a list of sets of states with no repeated entries, let $W$ be a list of pairs of a set of states and a letter, let $C$ be a set of states and $a$ a letter, and let $S = \{q : \delta(q, a) \in C\}$ be the preimage of $C$ under $a$. Then the waiting list after the splitter $(C, a)$, computed from the blocks $P$ and the rest…
nodes.title: Growth of the waiting list in one round

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA, $D$ a block of Hopcroft's final partition of $M$ and $p$ a state in $D$. Then a state $q$ lies in $D$ if and only if the language accepted by $M$ from $q$ equals the language accepted by $M$ from $p$.
nodes.title: Blocks of Hopcroft's partition are language classes

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$, two states $p$ and $q$ share a block of Hopcroft's final partition of $M$ exactly when the language accepted by $M$ from $p$ equals the language accepted by $M$ from $q$.
nodes.title: Correctness of Hopcroft's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of sets of states that is a partition into nonempty blocks, let $C$ be an entry of $P$, and let $p$ and $q$ be states lying in a common entry of $P$. Then $p \in C$ if and only if $q \in C$.
nodes.title: A block contains both or neither of two related states

nodes.summary: Every entry `newSplitters` adds for a block `D` is a half of `D` (one of the two sides of the split by `pre`), or the smaller half.
nodes.title: New splitters are halves of the split block

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ and reachable states $p$ and $q$ of $M$, the classes of $p$ and $q$ under Moore's equivalence on reachable states (the states of Moore's minimal automaton) are equal if and only if $p$ and $q$ share a block of Hopcroft's final partition of $M$.
nodes.title: Moore classes are Hopcroft blocks

nodes.summary: After `k` halving steps, the initial block is at least `2 ^ k` times the final block. The halving hypothesis is stated for the cardinalities only; no subset hypothesis is needed.
nodes.title: Halving chains shrink blocks by a factor of at least $2^k$

nodes.summary: Given a waiting list $W$ of pairs of a set of states and a letter and sets $S$ and $D$ of states, write $D_1 = D \cap S$ and $D_2 = D \setminus S$. The new waiting entries for $D$ consist, for each letter $b$ in the enumeration order of the alphabet, of both $(D_1, b)$ and $(D_2, b)$ if $(D, b)$ is in $W$, and otherwise of the single entry $(E, b)$, where $E$ is the smaller of $D_1$ and $D_2$ by cardinality ($D_1$…
nodes.title: New splitters for a split block

nodes.summary: Every popped splitter has a nonempty block, including splitters whose predecessor set is empty.
nodes.title: Popped Hopcroft splitters are nonempty

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with transition function $\delta$, a set $C$ of states and a letter $a$, the preimage of $C$ under $a$ is the set of states $q$ with $\delta(q, a) \in C$.
nodes.title: Preimage of a set under a letter

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with state set $Q$ and set of accepting states $F$, the rejecting block is the set $Q \setminus F$ of states of $M$ that are not accepting.
nodes.title: Rejecting states

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA and $P$ a list of blocks of states such that $P$ with the empty waiting list satisfies the invariants of Hopcroft's loop. Then two states $p$ and $q$ lie in a common block of $P$ if and only if they accept the same continuation languages, that is, $M$ accepts a word from $p$ exactly when it accepts it from $q$.
nodes.title: With an empty waiting list, blocks are the classes of equal continuation languages

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with transition function $\delta$, $P$ a list of blocks of states, $C$ a set of states and $a$ a letter. Two states $p$ and $q$ lie in a common block after the splitter $(C, a)$ is applied to $P$ if and only if they lie in a common block of $P$ and $\delta(p, a) \in C \iff \delta(q, a) \in C$.
nodes.title: Effect of one splitter on the common-block relation

nodes.summary: For a list $P$ of sets of states, two states $p$ and $q$ are related by $P$ when some block $D$ of $P$ contains both $p$ and $q$.
nodes.title: Lying in a common block

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with transition function $\delta$, a list $P$ of blocks of states, a set $C$ of states and a letter $a$, let $S = \{q : \delta(q, a) \in C\}$ be the preimage of $C$ under $a$. The partition after the splitter $(C, a)$ replaces each block $D$ of $P$, in order, by the two blocks $D \cap S$ and $D \setminus S$ when both are nonempty, and keeps $D$ otherwise.
nodes.title: One refinement round of the partition

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with transition function $\delta$, a list $P$ of blocks of states, a list $W$ of pairs of a set of states and a letter, a set $C$ of states and a letter $a$, let $S = \{q : \delta(q, a) \in C\}$ be the preimage of $C$ under $a$, and say that $S$ splits a set $D$ when $D$ meets both $S$ and its complement. The waiting list after the splitter $(C, a)$, from the rest $W$ of the waiting list, consists of…
nodes.title: One update of the waiting list

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA, $P$ a list of blocks of states, $W$ a list of pairs of a set of states and a letter, $C$ a set of states and $a$ a letter. If $P$ and the waiting list obtained by putting $(C, a)$ in front of $W$ satisfy the invariants of Hopcroft's loop, then so do the partition after the splitter $(C, a)$ and the waiting list after the splitter $(C, a)$ from the rest $W$.
nodes.title: One round preserves the invariants

nodes.summary: Let $S$ and $D$ be sets of states. Every piece of $D$ split by $S$ (the two sets $D \cap S$ and $D \setminus S$ if $D$ meets both $S$ and its complement, and $D$ itself otherwise) is contained in $S$ or disjoint from $S$: any two states $x$ and $y$ of the piece satisfy $x \in S \iff y \in S$.
nodes.title: Pieces of a split block lie on one side

nodes.summary: In a chain of blocks where each step at least halves the size, a block containing a given state can occur at most `Nat.log 2 n` times past the start, where `n` is the number of states. In Hopcroft's algorithm, the successive smaller halves containing one fixed state form such a chain: each of them is the smaller half of a split of the previous block containing that state.
nodes.title: The smaller-half counting lemma

nodes.summary: For finite sets $A$ and $B$ of states, the smaller one is $A$ if $|A| \le |B|$ and $B$ otherwise; on a tie in cardinality it is $A$.
nodes.title: Smaller of two finite sets of states

nodes.summary: For sets $P$ and $D$ of states, splitting $D$ by $P$ gives the two-element list $[D \cap P,\ D \setminus P]$ if both of these sets are nonempty, and the one-element list $[D]$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Splitting a block by a set

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of states is split by a set $P$ of states when $D$ contains both a state in $P$ and a state not in $P$, that is, when $D \cap P$ and $D \setminus P$ are both nonempty.
nodes.title: A set of states split by another

nodes.summary: Total state/letter charging along the actual execution. The bound includes initial tokens and tokens still pending through replacements. No amortized bound is assumed in the execution invariant.
nodes.title: Splitter count bound along a Hopcroft execution

nodes.summary: Each state is processed with a fixed letter at most `log₂ n + 1` times during any prefix of the actual initialized Hopcroft execution.
nodes.title: Hopcroft visits each of $n$ states at most $\log_2 n + 1$ times per letter

nodes.summary: Initially there is at most one token for each state and letter.
nodes.title: Initial splitter count is at most one

nodes.summary: Replacement contributes one token at a state in the parent block; otherwise only membership in the smaller half contributes a token.
nodes.title: Splitter count of newly added splitters

nodes.summary: A waiting entry supplies a token; duplicate entries remain counted.
nodes.title: Waiting entries give positive splitter count

nodes.summary: One refinement cannot increase logarithmic block-size credit plus pending-token credit. Replacing a pending splitter spends no new credit; adding a nonpending smaller half spends one logarithmic unit.
nodes.title: Potential inequality for one Hopcroft refinement round

nodes.summary: The exact token update at a state. Only its unique parent block can contribute a new token, even when other blocks split in the same round.
nodes.title: Splitter count update after one Hopcroft round

nodes.summary: Number of splitters with letter `b` containing `q`, with multiplicity. This applies both to the waiting list and to the actual popped trace.
nodes.title: Splitter count of a state and letter

nodes.summary: A refined block containing `q` is a subset of the old block containing `q`. Both partitions are the canonical Hopcroft partitions.
nodes.title: Refined Hopcroft blocks lie inside their old blocks

nodes.summary: A smaller-half entry added by `newSplitters` for a block `D` has at most half the size of `D`: the two halves are disjoint and union to `D`. No split hypothesis is needed: the halves of any block partition it.
nodes.title: Smaller-half splitters have at most half the block size

nodes.summary: If two disjoint sets union to `D`, the smaller of them has at most half the size of `D`.
nodes.title: The smaller part of a split has at most half the size

nodes.summary: The smaller of two sets has at most half their combined size: it is one of the two sets, so twice its size is at most the sum of the two sizes.
nodes.title: The smaller of two sets has at most half their total size
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
